name: ddcctl
desc: DDC monitor controls (brightness) for Mac OSX command-line
why: Talks DDC/CI over the display cable to control monitor settings, a hidden protocol door into your own screen.

brief.what_it_is: ddcctl is a command-line tool for macOS that adjusts an external monitor's built-in settings, starting with brightness and contrast, by sending DDC/CI commands over the display cable. You run it from the shell with a display number and a value, for example to set brightness or switch input source. The README says input source, speaker volume, RGB colors, color presets, and reset may also work, depending on how well the monitor's firmware implements them. Output is a change on the monitor itself, not a printed result.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a way to adjust your external monitor's built-in controls from the OSX shell, so you don't have to use the monitor's on-screen menu. It came from a TonyMac-x86 forum thread, and the author says it does what he needs on his own all-Apple setup.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the mechanism in detail. It says the code (ddcctl.m, with DDC.c reworked from jontaylor/DDC-CI-Tools-for-OS-X) sends DDC-controlled commands to the monitor. It also says a script can drive it, and that Alfred, ControlPlane, or Karabiner can call that script to switch presets.

commands_seen.context: Homebrew install, the first of three listed options (the README writes it as $ brew install ddcctl).
Example from the Input Sources section that sets display 1 to HDMI-1 (value 17).
Build from source after installing Xcode.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew (brew install ddcctl) is the first option. Alternatives are downloading ddcctl_binaries.zip from the GitHub releases page, or building from source: install Xcode, then run make. The README does not mention any extra runtimes, accounts, or first-run configuration. It does say the tool needs a Macintosh (not a hackintosh) and a DDC-controlled monitor.
brief.standout: The README is unusually candid. The author says the project is in maintenance mode, that he will not triage issues or run a support forum, and that he will only add features he can test on his own hardware. The input-source table, which maps values 1 to 27 to ports such as HDMI-1 (17) and USB-C (27), is a practical reference that many similar tools lack.
brief.status: The README says the project is in "maintenance mode" and that the author does not have time to triage new issues. No release date or last-commit date was visible in the fetched README, so I could not confirm recent activity. Status: maintenance mode, per the README's own statement.
brief.caveats: Maintenance mode: issues will not be triaged, and users are told to debug their own macOS and monitor problems and send fixes as PRs. Which settings work depends on the monitor's firmware. It is macOS-only, and the README says hackintosh setups are not the target. Licensed GPLv3. Building from source requires Xcode. The author's verification is manual, with no CI, and PRs are reviewed with no time estimate.
quotes: Adjust your external monitors' built-in controls from the OSX shell:
It is not a Community "Free Software" Project - its decidedly my personal utility and its in the (dreaded/loved) _"maintenance mode"_.
ddcctl currently does what _I need it to do_ on my own all-Apple fleet.
